title: Face Recognition Detective
summary: Place a difficulty at one component of a six-component model of recognising a person, and read the profile it produces. Then work backwards from six profiles to the component that would explain each.
learningObjectives: Say what each of six components contributes to recognising a person.
Read a profile of task outcomes backwards to the component that would explain it.
Use the voice route to decide whether a difficulty is confined to faces.
Recognise when a profile is compatible with more than one component, or with none.
List the explanations that come before any face-system account of a low score.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; everything runs in the browser tab. There is no self-test and no score for the reader, and the tool asks nothing about the person using it.
accessibilityNotes: Native radio, select and button controls, each with an accessible name (verified programmatically). The flow diagram is hidden from assistive technology and carries a visible sentence inside its own figure naming the affected component and what it does to each route; the affected box is crossed through and labelled 'affected' as well as being filled differently. The seven task outcomes are a list in which every item prints its own word - 'within range', 'impaired' or 'not administered' - so the left border is never the only carrier, and mismatches are marked with an attribute as well as a tint. A full table gives each task, what it asks for, the components it needs and its outcome. Each experiment has its own pinned primary and the inactive one is hidden; measured at 1366 by 768 the pins are 517px and 246px, and with the last control of either experiment scrolled to the bottom of the window the primary is still on screen. The schematic faces are decorative in the strict sense - nothing in the model depends on them - and are marked aria-hidden with their explanation in adjacent text. A live goal checklist writes '(met)' or '(not yet)' into the text. Every change announces through the shell's polite live region and focus moves to the model heading when the prediction unlocks it. Heading levels do not skip, forced colours are handled, and there is no horizontal page scroll at 320px, 375px, 1366px, 1440px or 1920px.
readmeTopic: Why recognising someone is several separable steps, how a voice task decides whether a difficulty is about faces, and when a profile has no answer
simulationNotes: Six components - general visual processing, face perception, face familiarity, voice recognition, person identity knowledge and name retrieval - arranged as two routes that converge on person identity knowledge and then on name retrieval. Seven tasks, each listing the components it needs: object discrimination needs general vision; face discrimination adds face perception; face familiarity adds familiarity; identity from the face adds person identity; name from the face adds name retrieval; identity from the voice needs voice recognition and person identity; name from the voice adds name retrieval. A task is impaired exactly when the affected component is one it needs. The model is all-or-nothing on purpose: it is a device for reasoning about patterns, not a simulation of severity. Six invented profiles: A fits face perception uniquely, B fits face familiarity, C fits person identity knowledge, D fits name retrieval, E fits nothing because every task is below range and any single component leaves something intact, and F fits both general visual processing and face perception because the non-face control task was not administered. The tool searches all six locations rather than asserting any of this. Schematic faces are generated from seven numbers - head width, chin width, eye spacing, eye height, eye size, nose length, mouth width - by mulberry32 from a visible seed starting at 20260807 and advancing by 1013 on each redraw. Deliberate simplifications: six components is fewer than the literature separates, whether familiarity is a stage at all is argued about, there is no severity, no day-to-day variation and no compensation from hair, gait, context or clothing. No published case, clinical measure or photograph is used, no anatomy is named, and nothing on the page assesses the reader.
